Basic ATC

Rullare verso

An ATC instruction authorizing an aircraft to proceed under its own power to a specified location on the aerodrome, such as a runway holding point or parking stand.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Rullare verso?

In this glossary, Rullare verso refers to: An ATC instruction authorizing an aircraft to proceed under its own power to a specified location on the aerodrome, such as a runway holding point or parking stand.

How is Rullare verso used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Terra, N123AB, richiede rullaggio al punto attesa pista 27 via Alpha."

Why does Rullare verso matter in aviation?

Rullare verso matters because it supports clear communication in Basic ATC contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Who uses Rullare verso?

Rullare verso is mainly used by Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew.

What category does Rullare verso belong to?

Definition

An ATC instruction authorizing an aircraft to proceed under its own power to a specified location on the aerodrome, such as a runway holding point or parking stand.

Operational example

Ground, N123AB, request taxi to holding point Runway 27 via Alpha.
